back: To work hard for a long time.
To lose your courage and decide not to do something.
To hurry up or cheer up (informal).
To reduce the amount of something (e.g., spending).
To think or talk about something unpleasant for too long.
To encourage someone to do something, usually something unwise.
To gradually end or fail in a disappointing way.
To succeed in communicating an idea.
To reach an agreement after long and difficult discussion.
To solve or settle small problems or details.
To suddenly stop doing something like a job or hobby (informal).
To start working hard, especially when you should have done it earlier.
To be honest and tell someone the truth about something.
